description:
src/lib.rs:83-95 defines a 'reg!' macro that wraps 6 method registrations (filenode.rs:98-115). The macro expands a closure with four arguments (, , , ), discards  via '_ci', and just calls one handler. Six call sites, all identical except for the method name and handler fn.

The macro indirection costs the reader: each macro invocation reads as 'reg!("FileNode/get", backend, |b, _ci, a, ctx| { handle_filenode_get(&*b, &ctx, a).await })'. The reader has to look up the macro to see that this is just 'register a method that takes (Arc<B>, _, args, ctx)'.

A function-shaped helper from jmap_server (perhaps register_handler<B, F, Fut>(...)) would be more readable:

  dispatcher.register("FileNode/get", ClosureHandler::new(backend.clone(), |b, _, a, ctx| async move { handle_filenode_get(&*b, &ctx, a).await }.boxed()));

Then no macro. Each line is self-contained for a reader.

Alternatively: keep the macro but inline its body so the closure shape is obvious at the call site. Either way, the current shape is slightly worse than the alternatives.

Flag opinion: this is a style call. Mark as opinion if the canonical sibling jmap-mail-server uses the same reg! pattern (cookie-cutter rule). Defer to whichever is the canonical.
title: Two near-identical patches construction blocks in src/lib.rs reg! macro
